definitions.explanation: Describes a tendency to engage with the outside world, embrace new connections, or focus on external matters. Used for personalities, organizations, or national policies.

examples.japanese: {外向|そとむ}きな{性格|せいかく}の{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: She's a person with an outgoing personality.

examples.japanese: もっと{外向|そとむ}きの{経営|けいえい}{戦略|せんりゃく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: We need a more outward-looking business strategy.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}は{外向|そとむ}きの{姿勢|しせい}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}し、{海外|かいがい}{市場|しじょう}の{開拓|かいたく}に{力|ちから}を{入|い}れている。
examples.english: The government has adopted an outward-looking stance and is putting effort into developing overseas markets.

notes:
The counterpart of {内向|うちむ}き. Used for both personal disposition (extroverted, sociable) and broader orientations of organizations or nations (internationally engaged, open to the world).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外向|そとむ}きな{性格|せいかく}: outgoing personality
- {外向|そとむ}きな{姿勢|しせい}: outward-looking stance
- {外向|そとむ}き{志向|しこう}: outward-oriented tendency

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {外向的|がいこうてき}: extroverted — specifically for personality; more psychological
- {内向|うちむ}き: inward-looking — the direct opposite
- {積極的|せっきょくてき}: proactive; positive — implies willingness to take action
